main_text.p: Quaest.cxv. passim Epistolam ad Hebraeos ut Canonicam in subsidium vocat, autho-re quanquam, suo sane more, tacito. Ita Libro II. adversus Haer. C.xv. citat verba Hebr.1.3. faciens omnia verbo virtutis suae. L. IV. C.xxi. adducit locum, Hebr. VIII.8,9. Ecce disponam Testamentum novum &c. L.v. C.v. ex loco Hebr.xi.5. Quoniam quidem Enoch placens Deo, in quo placuit corpore translatus est. Praeterea Eusebius, Hist.Eccles. L.v. C.xxv. ubi de scriptis Irenaei, meminisse dicit exer-tim, in scripto quodam variarum disquisitionum, [illegible, ~20 letters] Excipi tamen potest illud Stephani Tritheitae, apud Photium in Bibliotheca Cod.CCXXXII [illegible, ~30 letters] Hippolytus & Irenaeus, Epistolam Pauli ad Hebraeos, illius esse ne-gant. Qua vero fide id de Irenaeo asserat Tritheita, docent alia ejusdem plura fa-bulosa, inepta, falsa; ut Photius illum etiam [illegible, ~12 letters] infimulet. Forte quia

page.notes: The Greek phrases in the first and fourth lines are too blurred to read reliably, so I have marked them illegible. The Greek word after "etiam" is also doubtful. The reference "VIII.8,9" is read as "VIII.8,a." on the scan, since the mark after 8 is unclear; the printed form is kept as far as I can read it. The "9" and the "a." are uncertain. The first Greek line appears to be a quotation of Eusebius, and the second a reference to Photius, Bibl. Cod. 232.
